subject: Onboarding runbook: proxying + SCIM + service-account patterns for IP allowlist cutover
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.p@auroramed.com>, IT Security <it-sec@auroramed.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 13:04:00 -0700
Subject: Onboarding runbook: proxying + SCIM + service-account patterns for IP allowlist cutover

Hi Raj / AuroraMed security team —

Thanks again for the kickoff earlier. To keep momentum and avoid surprises during the SSO/SCIM cutover, I put together a lightweight runbook and a proposed proxying strategy for your environment. The goal is threefold: (1) enable SAML SSO and SCIM provisioning without breaking existing IP-restricted flows, (2) provide a clear service-account naming and permission pattern for automation, and (3) define a fallback/proxy plan during the first-week cutover window.

Attachments: onboard-checklist-v1.pdf, mutual-action-plan.xlsx (see short summary below).

Quick asks to close out before we lock the cutover window: 
- Can you share the exact outbound CIDR ranges for your integration (we'll add to our allowlist)?
- Please send SAML metadata or IdP endpoints (entityID / ACS URL) and SCIM base URL and auth method.
- Confirm whether AuroraMed requires a dedicated service account per environment (prod/staging) or a single cross-env account.

Proposed timeline: 
- Dry run (canary) on staging: 2 business days after we receive SAML metadata and IPs
- Prod cutover window requested: 2026-09-02 02:00–06:00 UTC (we can shift to your preferred slot)

Runbook highlights (attached):
- Staging proxy flow: temporarily route outbound traffic from Redwood through a short-lived proxy endpoint that lives in AuroraMed's VPC so SAML assertions and SCIM calls originate from an allowed IP.
- Service accounts: recommend pattern aurora-redwood-sa-{env} with minimal RBAC (provisioner + webhook-runner).
- Fallback: if certs/ACS mismatch during cutover, fallback to a request-level redirect back to legacy auth for 15 minutes while we triage.

Irene
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0149

From: Raj Patel <raj.p@auroramed.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: IT Security <it-sec@auroramed.com>, Procurement <procurement@auroramed.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding runbook: proxying + SCIM + service-account patterns for IP allowlist cutover

Irene —

Thanks for the clear plan and checklist. A couple quick answers and notes from our side: 
- Outbound CIDR ranges: 34.120.0.0/18, 34.121.64.0/18 (these are our egress ranges for the integration layer).
- SAML: attaching our IdP metadata (see auroramed-saml-metadata.xml) — ACS URL is https://sso.auroramed.com/saml/acs, entityID is https://idp.auroramed.com/; we run signed assertions and expect SP-initiated flows.
- SCIM: base URL is https://scim.auroramed.com/v2/ with token-based auth (bearer token we'll share via secure link)
- Service accounts: we prefer separate service accounts per environment (prod/staging). Security wants distinct credentials and clear rotation windows.

We can do the staging dry run the week of 2026-08-31. Procurement will need the mutual action plan signed before prod cutover — looping them in.

Thanks,
Raj
Director, IT Integrations | AuroraMed
raj.p@auroramed.com | +1 212-555-0199

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding runbook: proxying + SCIM + service-account patterns for IP allowlist cutover

Thanks Raj — good detail. Ben, can you validate the proxy approach and confirm whether our ephemeral proxy endpoint can be hosted in AuroraMed's subnet (we prefer that) or if we should stand up a temporary NAT in our account and ask AuroraMed to allowlist our egress?

Also: procurement asks about a standard T&Cs addendum for IP-restricted integrations. Marissa, can you confirm the template we usually send?

Monica
Sr. Implementation Lead | Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Raj Patel <raj.p@auroramed.com>, IT Security <it-sec@auroramed.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding runbook: proxying + SCIM + service-account patterns for IP allowlist cutover

Raj / AuroraMed security —

Couple technical notes from our infra side: 
1) Hosting proxy in your VPC: preferred for shortest path and avoids wide allowlisting. We'll provide a small ami + init script; you'll create a jump host (t3.small) in a private subnet with an outbound NAT and an IAM role that permits us to register the proxy with our control plane. This keeps egress IPs stable.
2) If you cannot host, fallback is Redwood-managed NAT with our ephemeral egress IPs (we'll provide the /32s 24 hours before the window).
3) SCIM throttling: we'll default to 10 rps; please confirm if your SCIM endpoint can sustain that during initial provisioning.
4) Service-account pattern: aurora-redwood-sa-prod (scim:write, sso:webhook) and aurora-redwood-sa-stg (scim:write) — rotation policy 90 days; we can integrate with your KMS for key escrow.

Security question: do you require mTLS for SCIM or will bearer token be sufficient? If mTLS is required we need cert details and the CA chain.

Ben
Infra Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: Raj Patel <raj.p@auroramed.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.com>
Cc: IT Security <it-sec@auroramed.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@auroramed.com>
Date: Wed, 26 Aug 2026 16:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Onboarding runbook: proxying + SCIM + service-account patterns for IP allowlist cutover

Ben / team —

We can host the proxy in our VPC. I'll have our network engineer create a private subnet and a jump host and share the subnet id and egress NAT details by 2026-08-27 12:00 UTC.

Answers:
- SCIM: bearer token is fine for now (no mTLS). We'll confirm sustained throughput — our team says 15 rps is fine for provisioning bursts.
- Service-account rotation: 90 days ok. We'll create separate roles per env and provide SSM Parameter Store paths for secrets.
- I've uploaded the SAML metadata to our secure share (link: https://drive.company/auroramed/sso/auroramed-saml-metadata.xml) and added the requested CIDR ranges to your onboarding doc.

Procurement: we can sign the mutual action plan; please send the DocuSign powerform link and an invoice to procurement@auroramed.com.

I'll be available during the dry run window; please pencil in 2026-09-01 22:00 UTC for a final pre-cutover run.

Thanks,
Raj
